clue.text: Cared about what grew in Lebanon?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the word cared are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cared about a crop grown in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the anagram of CARED. The tree is on Lebanon's flag, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is the famous tree of Lebanon's mountains, pictured on its national flag.

clue.text: He will shoot in action

parts.note: sounds like a soldier firing in battle but means a person filming scenes when the director calls action

explanation.definitionFit: A person who operates a film camera shoots scenes.

clue.text: Fair drive for Dawkins?

parts.note: a funfair ride of small bumper cars, linked to Jack Dawkins, the Artful Dodger in Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dawkins is the Artful Dodger, so these cars suit him by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper cars at a funfair, steered to dodge or hit one another.

clue.text: Music with words all the way through

definitions.meaning: a style of loud popular music

definitions.text: with words all the way through
definitions.meaning: a British seaside stick of hard candy with a town's name running through it

explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a hard sugar stick sold at British resorts, with the resort's name printed through its length.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of popular music, and also seaside candy sticks lettered right through.

clue.text: Bill left, being paid off

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
quitted is an older past tense of quit, meaning left

explanation.surface: A bill was left unpaid, or was settled after all.
explanation.walkthrough: To acquit a debt is an old phrase for settling it, so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit once meant to discharge a debt, so something acquitted has been settled in full.

clue.text: Enquiry-form with square one in it, to be resolved

indicators.note: to be resolved means the letters of square one in it must be worked out into their right order

explanation.surface: A form of enquiry containing a basic question that still needs solving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be resolved' signals the anagram of SQUAREONEINIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed list of questions used to gather information.

clue.text: Terrible fellow elected around Virginia

indicators.note: around says the word for elected goes outside the abbreviation

parts.note: a party elected is said to be in
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: An awful man is elected somewhere in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' is not an adjective but part of a title: Ivan the Terrible, the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsar Ivan IV of Russia is known by the epithet the Terrible.

clue.text: Theatre converted at that time

indicators.note: a converted building is changed into something else, so the letters of theatre are reordered

explanation.surface: A theatre was converted at that point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' gives the anagram of THEATRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning then, or on that account.

clue.text: Spy-leader in assignment that is dirty

indicators.note: in says the spy's first letter is placed inside the word for assignment

parts.note: a duty is a task or assignment

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A spymaster on a mission that is grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy-leader' gives S, which goes into DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in dust, so grubby or unclean.

clue.text: Examination partially performed, I calm down

indicators.note: partially says only part of the run of words performed, I calm supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A doctor's check-up is half done and the patient calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'performED I CALm'; 'down' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A check-up by a doctor is called a medical in Britain.

clue.text: Fair game from joke-shop reserves?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a shop's supply of items that cause laughs

explanation.definitionFit: A target of mockery is legitimate prey, and literally a supply of things causing laughter.

clue.text: Coats made by seal-men, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the seal-men are in a bad way, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coats are made by sorrowful seal hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' gives the anagram of SEALMEN. 'Coats' is a verb-like noun: layers of paint or glaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels are glossy layers of paint or glaze applied as coatings.

clue.text: Long grass reveals animal on its back

indicators.note: an animal lying on its back is turned over, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: Long grass reveals an animal lying on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on its back' turns DEER around.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a tall grass-like plant growing in wet places.

clue.text: Set of musical chairs?

parts.note: a set of matching furniture, playing on a set of pieces in music

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a matching set of furniture and a set of instrumental movements.

clue.text: Extremely light

definitions.meaning: an intensifier meaning to a great degree
a flare fired from a pistol

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an intensifier like hugely, and also names a signal flare shot into the sky.

clue.text: Uses needles to raise a row

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it upwards, writing it backwards

parts.note: a row or fuss is a stink, as in raising a stink

explanation.surface: Someone uses needles to start a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns STINK upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Working yarn with needles into a fabric.

clue.text: Perfect interval for Beethoven's Emperor' concerto?

definitions.meaning: in music theory a perfect interval spanning five notes
the Emperor is Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5

explanation.definitionFit: A musical gap of five scale notes, and the ordinal of Beethoven's last piano concerto.

clue.text: Mini-shorts apt to make one cynical about mankind

indicators.note: to make says the letters of mini-shorts apt are reworked to form something new

explanation.surface: Wearing mini-shorts is likely to turn someone sour about humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' signals the anagram of MINISHORTSAPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who distrusts or dislikes humanity in general.

clue.text: Begged for cheese-spread in flower-garden

indicators.note: in places the jumbled cheese inside the flower bed

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden for flowers

indicators.note: spread treats cheese as being spread about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded for a cheese spread in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' makes SEECHE from CHEESE, which goes 'in' BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleaded urgently; an alternative past tense of a verb meaning implore.

clue.text: Old scourge never used, presumably, in Isle of Man?

definitions.text: Old scourge never used, presumably, in Isle of Man?

parts.words: Old scourge never used, presumably, in Isle of Man?
parts.note: a flogging whip of knotted cords, joked about because Manx cats have no tails

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is famous for the Manx cat, which is born without a tail, so a whip named after a cat's tails would be out of place there.
explanation.definitionFit: This whip of nine knotted cords was once used for naval and prison floggings.

clue.text: Business interest

definitions.meaning: something that matters to a person

explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a firm, and a matter of concern is something one cares about.

clue.text: He won't thank you for tearing about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of tearing are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An ungrateful man rushes off without thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives the anagram of TEARING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person, one who shows no thanks.

clue.text: Facility for being crooked

explanation.definitionFit: A knack for something is a natural inclination, and the same word means twisted or corrupt.

clue.text: Graduate has equipment brought up for fabric-dyeing

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing a word up writes it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: kit is equipment

explanation.surface: A graduate brings up gear for dyeing cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns KIT around in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax-resist method of dyeing cloth from Indonesia.

clue.text: Screen dancer reported on the move

indicators.note: reported says the dancer's name is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Fred Astaire was the great Hollywood dancer

explanation.surface: A film dancer is said to be moving about.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire's surname, spoken, gives the word for up and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, moving or in motion.

clue.text: Bogeyman of uncommon gore

indicators.note: uncommon means the word gore is not in its usual form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommon' gives the anagram of GORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster from folk tales, a frightening figure like a bogeyman.

clue.text: Space for Othello to get up?

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: Shakespeare's Othello is the Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: An actor playing Othello needs space to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello is a Moor; 'to get up' reverses MOOR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means space, as in room to move.

clue.text: Strength of objection

explanation.definitionFit: The word means muscular power and, informally, a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Musical ornament not necessarily reserved for quaver

definitions.text: Musical ornament not necessarily reserved for quaver

parts.words: Musical ornament not necessarily reserved for quaver
parts.note: a rapid wavering effect in music, which can be played on notes of any length, not only short quavers

explanation.walkthrough: A quaver is both a short note and a trembling of the voice; the effect can be used on any note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremulous, wavering effect in singing or playing, used as decoration.

clue.text: I use 19 across, would you say, of one having a flutter?

indicators.note: would you say tells the solver that the pronoun I is heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
to use a whip is to lash

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they would flog a gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is the whip; using it means to lash. A flutter is a small bet, but here it is the blinking of an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair on the eyelid's edge, which moves when someone blinks quickly or flirts.

clue.text: Description of Warwick's powerful official

definitions.meaning: the Earl of Warwick in the Wars of the Roses was nicknamed for setting monarchs on the throne
someone with influence over who takes high office

explanation.definitionFit: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, was known for deposing and installing kings, and the word now means any power broker.

clue.text: Discover, full of energy, a demon

indicators.note: full of says the word for discover holds another letter inside it

parts.note: to find is to discover
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts E inside FIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an evil spirit or devil.
